claims.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
claims.evidence: Orient every independently transformed card from its hoop to its ball. The swish condition gives indegree=outdegree=1 at each occupied position and zero at every other position, so the transformed arcs are a disjoint union of directed simple cycles. Each component uses a subset of the physical cards and is itself a swish. Conversely, a realizable directed simple cycle puts exactly one hoop and one ball at each of its vertices. Restricting each type's usage to its number of physical copies gives exactly the stated multiplicity constraint.
claims.witness: The two implications are witnessed respectively by taking any cycle component of a swish and by overlaying the cards realizing the arcs of any directed simple cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the source definition, independently checked against the complete finite 4-by-3 transformation model; no web or external material used.

claims.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
claims.evidence: The four position orbits have sizes 4,2,4,2. Exact enumeration gives internal-type counts 3,1,3,1 and 28 cross types in 14 reversal pairs. Both members of a cross reversal pair realize a directed 2-cycle, so at most 14 cross types may occur. On either four-position orbit, its three internal types realize a directed triangle, so at most two may occur; each two-position orbit has only one internal type. Hence the support bound is 14+2+2+1+1=20. For equality, order the four position orbits, choose all 14 cross types directed forward, two internal types on each four-position orbit, and the unique type on each two-position orbit. Cross arcs strictly increase the orbit rank, while the selected internal cards cannot form a cycle.
claims.witness: The checker constructs the stated 20-type collection and exhaustively finds no realizable directed simple cycle.
claims.search_method: Enumerated all ordered distinct position pairs modulo the four grid symmetries, classified reversal pairs and internal types, and verified the extremal construction by exact cycle search.

claims.claim: Unless all eight internal types are duplicated, the usual once-or-twice interpretation of the 60-card deck already yields a 29-card no-swish subset.
claims.evidence: If k of the eight internal types are doubled, their physical-card count is 8+k. When k≤7, at least 60-(8+k)≥45 cards are cross-orbit cards. Every cross card is forward in exactly 12 of the 24 total orders of the four position orbits. Thus some order selects at least ceil((52-k)/2) forward cross cards, which is at least 23 when k≤7. Adding the six cycle-free internal cards gives at least 29. Orbit rank is nondecreasing on internal arcs and strictly increases on every selected cross arc, so this collection has no directed cycle.
claims.witness: The worst case is k=7: six safe internal cards plus ceil(45/2)=23 forward cross cards gives 29.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of all 24 orbit orders verified the half-forward incidence for every cross type; the remaining argument is integer averaging.

claims.claim: The direct orbit-order construction yields 29 cards unless all eight internal types are doubled and duplicated cross types are direction-balanced between every pair of position orbits.
claims.evidence: With all eight internal types doubled, exactly 16 of the 28 cross types are doubled. For an orbit order π, let S(π) count doubled cross types directed forward. Every doubled type is forward in 12 of 24 orders, so the average score is 8. If d_ij differs from d_ji for some orbit pair, choose an order where i,j are adjacent and swap them; all other pair contributions remain fixed while their contribution changes, proving S is nonconstant. Since its integer average is 8, some score is at least 9, and the construction has 6+14+9=29 cards. If every d_ij=d_ji, every order instead has score 8 and this template has 28. The proof correctly makes no assertion that another construction cannot reach 29 in the balanced case.
claims.witness: The checker exhausts all feasible count vectors with 16 doubled cross types: 186 balanced and 148392 unbalanced vectors. Every balanced vector has all scores 8, and every unbalanced vector has maximum score at least 9.
claims.search_method: Combined the adjacent-swap proof with exhaustive exact enumeration over all feasible direction-count vectors and all 24 orbit orders.

claims.claim: The authorized input omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target.
claims.evidence: The source states that the commercial deck has 60 cards and 36 transformation types but supplies no 36-entry multiplicity vector. Two once-or-twice vectors compatible with those aggregates give opposite answers. Deck X starts with one of every type and doubles all eight internal types plus both directions in eight cross reversal pairs. Any no-swish subset then has at most six internal cards, at most two cards from each of those eight pairs, and at most one from each remaining pair, totaling 28; the forward construction attains 28. Deck Y doubles nine forward cross types, all 14 reverse types, and one internal type. Its six safe internal cards, two copies of the nine selected forward types, and one copy of the other five forward types form a 29-card no-swish subset. Both decks have exactly 60 cards, 36 types, and multiplicities one or two.
claims.witness: Deck X has certified maximum 6+8·2+6=28. Deck Y has an explicit cycle-free witness of size 6+9·2+5=29.
claims.search_method: Constructed both multiplicity vectors within the independently enumerated type system, checked their totals and multiplicities exactly, proved Deck X's upper bound, and performed exact cycle searches on both witnesses.

target_evidence: The draft proves substantial structural and conditional results, including a sharp support bound and broad sufficient conditions for a 29-card no-swish subset. It also rigorously demonstrates that the aggregate deck information in the authorized source cannot determine the answer. It does not, however, provide the actual commercial deck's multiplicity vector, exhibit a 29-card subset of that deck, or certify a 28-card upper bound for that deck. Therefore it does not fully resolve the exact target, and its explicit PARTIAL claim is accurate.
